claims.body: The Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Hurricanes are the best at keeping shots away. Hot take: the Hurricanes shut it down.

claims.head: Tilted ice, toward the Flames’ net
claims.body: At 5-on-5, the Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Flames near the bottom. The ice should tilt the Hurricanes’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

notes.text: Taylor Hall is out (upper-body injury) and missed their last game. Bradly Nadeau has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 3 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.
Bradly Nadeau was added to the roster on Oct 15 and has played beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake.
Felix Unger Sörum was added to the roster on Oct 17 and has played beside Eric Robinson and Jesperi Kotkaniemi.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 32% of the team’s shorthanded time in 9 games, up from 1% last season.

faceoff.text: Jordan Staal is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 42% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 20 seconds at a time, against 65 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Nikolaj Ehlers (17 of 20 changes).

notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 7 games cover only 29% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fourth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 42%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Martin Pospíšil has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 7 games, up from 2% last season.

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the Metropolitan with 15 points, the Flames tied for seventh in the Pacific with 2 points.

CGY.head: The Hurricanes should be favored
CGY.body: Even though Carolina is on the second night of a back-to-back and Calgary has home-ice advantage, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. To pull this off, the Flames can start with getting good looks, plus Devin Cooley stealing the show.

CAR.head: A big edge for the Hurricanes
CAR.body: Even though Carolina is on the second night of a back-to-back and Calgary has home-ice advantage, the Hurricanes have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. If the Flames want to spoil it, start with getting good looks.

story.head: The Hurricanes are rolling
paras: The Hurricanes have won seven straight, and they’re rolling. The Flames are 1-6-0.

It’s strength against strength: the Flames are one of the league’s best for shot volume, but the Hurricanes are the best at keeping shots away. The Canes usually control more of the chances than the Flames do.

items.text: The Hurricanes are newly without Taylor Hall, and have been without Jordan Staal since Oct 10.
The Flames have been without Samuel Honzek and Joel Hanley for several games, and have had to make do without Jonathan Huberdeau all season.
Mark Jankowski has scored in six straight games.
Mikael Backlund is two points from passing Johnny Gaudreau for fifth on the Flames’ all-time scoring list.
